sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店打碟的黑胶唱片时代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, Capitol Hill, shrouded in secrecy and following its own set of rules, becomes the latest center of power to come under scrutiny for sexual harassment.
sentences.zh: 今天，国会山——这个笼罩在秘密之中并遵循自身规则的地方——成为了因性骚扰而受到审查的最新权力中心。

sentences.en: And Senator Kirsten Gillibrand on being a woman in Congress in this moment.
sentences.zh: 以及参议员克里斯汀·吉利布兰德谈论此时此刻作为一名国会女性的感受。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, November 21St.
sentences.zh: 今天是11月21日，星期二。

sentences.en: Katie Rogers, when did Congress realize that it had to evaluate its own role in this cultural moment around sexual harassment?
sentences.zh: 凯蒂·罗杰斯，国会是什么时候意识到它必须评估自己在当前围绕性骚扰的文化时刻中所扮演的角色？

sentences.en: You can really think about the reporting that The New York Times has done on Harvey Weinstein spreading eastward from Hollywood to the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 你可以认为《纽约时报》关于哈维·韦恩斯坦的报道正从好莱坞向东蔓延至国会山。

sentences.en: I think in some ways it was a matter of time just because Washington and Hollywood have similar power dynamics.
sentences.zh: 我认为在某种程度上这只是时间问题，因为华盛顿和好莱坞有着相似的权力动态。

sentences.en: I now call to order the Committee on House Administration for purposes of today's hearing titled Preventing Sexual Harassment in the Workplace.
sentences.zh: 我现在宣布众议院行政委员会会议开始，今天听证会的主题是“防止职场性骚扰”。

sentences.en: One of the results of the increased scrutiny on sexual harassment and workplace violations of that nature on Capitol Hill was a hearing last Tuesday held by the House Administration Committee.
sentences.zh: 对国会山性骚扰和此类职场违规行为的审查力度加大，其结果之一就是众议院行政委员会上周二举行了一场听证会。

sentences.en: There is no place for sexual harassment in our society, period, and especially in Congress.
sentences.zh: 我们的社会中绝无性骚扰的容身之地，句号，在国会更是如此。

sentences.en: It was a pretty stunning, unusual hearing for Capitol Hill.
sentences.zh: 对于国会山来说，这真是一场令人震惊且不同寻常的听证会。

sentences.en: Today we'll hear from two members.
sentences.zh: 今天我们将听取两位议员的发言。

sentences.en: What sort of testimony was there at this hearing?
sentences.zh: 这次听证会上有什么样的证词？

sentences.en: Thank you, Mr. Chairman.
sentences.zh: 谢谢主席先生。

sentences.en: Congresswoman Barbara Comstock, she's a Republican of Virginia, spoke out about a male lawmaker.
sentences.zh: 来自弗吉尼亚州的共和党众议员芭芭拉·康斯托克公开谈论了一位男性议员。

sentences.en: This is about a member who is here now.
sentences.zh: 这涉及一位目前仍在任的议员。

sentences.en: Tricking a young woman into showing up at his home.
sentences.zh: 诱骗一名年轻女性到他家中。

sentences.en: This member asked a staffer to bring them over some materials to their residence.
sentences.zh: 这位议员要求一名工作人员把一些材料送到他的住所。

sentences.en: And then opened the door in a towel.
sentences.zh: 然后只围着一条浴巾就开了门。

sentences.en: At that point, he decided to expose himself.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，他决定暴露自己。

sentences.en: She left, and then she quit her job.
sentences.zh: 她离开了，随后辞去了工作。

sentences.en: And then...
sentences.zh: 然后……

sentences.en: There are two members of Congress, Republican and Democrat, right now, who serve, who have engaged in sexual harassment.
sentences.zh: 目前有两位国会议员，一男一女，分别来自共和党和民主党，他们都曾参与过性骚扰。

sentences.en: Congresswoman Jackie Speier, she's a Democrat of California.
sentences.zh: 来自加利福尼亚州的民主党众议员杰基·斯皮尔。

sentences.en: These harasser propositions such as, are you going to be a good girl, to perpetrators exposing their genitals, to victims having their private parts grabbed on the House floor.
sentences.zh: 这些骚扰者的行为从问“你是不是个乖女孩”，到加害者暴露生殖器，再到受害者在众议院大厅被抓私处，应有尽有。

sentences.en: Are these all female lawmakers coming forward with stories of what happened to staff members?
sentences.zh: 这些都是女性议员站出来讲述发生在工作人员身上的故事吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so it's mostly female lawmakers relaying these stories because, I mean,
sentences.zh: 是的，所以大部分都是女性议员在转述这些故事，因为，我的意思是，

sentences.en: they are at a point where they have acquired enough power on Capitol Hill that they can actually point out the wrongdoing, speak on behalf of their staffers,
sentences.zh: 她们已经达到了在国会山拥有足够权力的地步，可以真正指出不当行为，并代表她们的工作人员发声，

sentences.en: many of whom are terrified to speak up on this issue.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人对谈论这个问题感到恐惧。

sentences.en: Katie, walk us through how we're learning that this system actually works in Congress when someone has a complaint or an allegation.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，请带我们了解一下，当有人提出投诉或指控时，国会的这套系统实际上是如何运作的。

sentences.en: Right, so when somebody has a complaint, what's interesting is that it's not even called a complaint if they go to the Office of Compliance.
sentences.zh: 好的，当有人提出投诉时，有趣的是，如果他们去合规办公室，这甚至不被称为投诉。

sentences.en: It's called a request for counseling.
sentences.zh: 它被称为咨询请求。

sentences.en: You then have mandatory counseling for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 然后你必须进行为期30天的强制咨询。

sentences.en: Typically, it's a 30-day period, which is sort of an intake period of assessing what the problem is and what needs to be done going forward.
sentences.zh: 通常这是一个30天的周期，算是一个评估问题所在以及未来需要做什么的接收期。

sentences.en: After that, you are required, and I underscore required, to sign a non-disclosure agreement before you even begin mediation.
sentences.zh: 在此之后，你被要求——我强调是“被要求”——在开始调解之前签署一份保密协议。

sentences.en: There's a period of mediation.
sentences.zh: 接下来有一个调解期。

sentences.en: It's confidential.
sentences.zh: 它是保密的。

sentences.en: There's very little visibility into what happens during this phase.
sentences.zh: 在这个阶段发生的事情几乎没有任何透明度。

sentences.en: That's another 30 days.
sentences.zh: 那是另外30天。

sentences.en: I might also add that during that process, the victim can't even communicate that they are going through an OOC process to their family, to their friends,
sentences.zh: 我还想补充一点，在这个过程中，受害者甚至不能告诉家人、朋友，

sentences.en: or to anyone in their religious community.
sentences.zh: 或者宗教社区里的任何人，他们正在经历合规办公室的流程。

sentences.en: And Katie, when you say mediation, do you mean mediation between the accuser and the accused?
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，当你提到调解时，是指控诉者和被控诉者之间的调解吗？

sentences.en: Yes, and the Office of Compliance says that 40-50% of cases are settled during this time.
sentences.zh: 是的，合规办公室表示，40%到50%的案件在此期间达成和解。

sentences.en: If mediation fails, and the next step would be to file a claim in federal court or file an appeal request, there's another 30 days of waiting, which is called a cooling-off period,
sentences.zh: 如果调解失败，下一步将是在联邦法院提起诉讼或提出上诉请求，这中间还有30天的等待期，被称为“冷静期”，

sentences.en: before that official complaint going to court or asking for an appeal can be filed.
sentences.zh: 在此之后才能正式提起诉讼或要求上诉。

sentences.en: So now 90 days have elapsed, and that employee is still required to work in that legislative office.
sentences.zh: 所以现在已经过去了90天，而那名员工仍然被要求在那个立法办公室工作。

sentences.en: And then during this mediation phase, the person's day has to go on as normal as this is happening.
sentences.zh: 而且在调解阶段，当这一切发生时，当事人的生活必须照常进行。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: What does that mean?
sentences.zh: 那意味着什么？

sentences.en: It means they have to keep going to work every day going through this process.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们必须每天继续去上班，经历这个过程。

sentences.en: And that may mean potentially getting through the day working alongside the person that a staff member has accused.
sentences.zh: 这可能意味着每天都要和被工作人员指控的那个人一起工作。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the overarching rule for all of this, too, is that if somebody wants to register a counseling request, I guess, and start this process,
sentences.zh: 而且这一切的总体规则是，如果有人想登记咨询请求，我想，并开始这个过程，

sentences.en: it has to be no later than 180 days after the episode occurred or the abuse occurred.
sentences.zh: 必须在事件发生或虐待发生后的180天内提出。

sentences.en: So you're dealing with at least three months before you get to an official complaint, and you have to do this within 180 days after something happens to you.
sentences.zh: 所以你在正式投诉之前至少要处理三个月的时间，而且你必须在事情发生后的180天内完成这一切。

sentences.en: And really, at the heart of this, too, is that if you're accusing a lawmaker of abuse, they have house counsel,
sentences.zh: 而且真正核心的问题在于，如果你指控一名议员虐待，他们有众议院法律顾问，

sentences.en: which means a government lawyer will be working for them on behalf of their office and the institution of Congress.
sentences.zh: 这意味着政府律师将代表他们的办公室和国会机构为他们工作。

sentences.en: And then the person who has filed the complaint can either go forward without an attorney or must figure out how to be represented.
sentences.zh: 而提交投诉的人要么只能在没有律师的情况下继续，要么必须自己想办法找代理律师。

sentences.en: And during the course of my reporting on this, I've talked to lawyers all over Washington.
sentences.zh: 在报道这件事的过程中，我和华盛顿各地的律师谈过。

sentences.en: A lot of people just can't financially get through this process.
sentences.zh: 很多人在经济上根本无法支撑这个过程。

sentences.en: So a lot of people don't even go through it.
sentences.zh: 所以很多人甚至根本不去尝试。

sentences.en: So it's really no wonder that staffers do not seek this process at all.
sentences.zh: 所以难怪工作人员根本不寻求这个流程。

sentences.en: There is zero accountability and zero transparency.
sentences.zh: 这里完全没有问责制，也没有透明度。

sentences.en: So Congress provides and pays for a lawyer to the accused lawmaker, but not the staffer, who's also a government employee, making the complaint.
sentences.zh: 所以国会为被指控的议员提供并支付律师费用，但却不为同样是政府雇员、提出投诉的工作人员支付。

sentences.en: Taxpayers foot the bill and the harasser goes on with his or her life.
sentences.zh: 纳税人买单，而骚扰者继续过他或她的生活。

sentences.en: The present system may have been OK in the dark ages.
sentences.zh: 目前的制度在黑暗时代可能还可以。

sentences.en: It is not appropriate for the 21st century.
sentences.zh: 但它不适合21世纪。

sentences.en: Katie, how did the women that you spoke to describe this process and their experience with it?
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，你采访的女性是如何描述这个过程以及她们的经历的？

sentences.en: My colleague Yamiche Alcindor and I talked to two people who have gone through this.
sentences.zh: 我和我的同事亚米切·阿尔辛多采访了两个经历过这一切的人。

sentences.en: We do not know a lot and we can't say a lot about what these people have gone through based on how tightly these nondisclosures are wrapped around them.
sentences.zh: 我们了解的不多，也不能说太多关于这些人经历了什么，因为保密协议对他们束缚得太紧了。

sentences.en: What I can say is that both people described it as a re-traumatizing experience for them because it forced them to relive this period of their lives and answer the same set of questions repeatedly over a period of months.
sentences.zh: 我能说的是，两人都将其描述为一种重温创伤的经历，因为它迫使她们重温那段生活，并在几个月的时间里反复回答同样的问题。

sentences.en: So they're describing a system that seems to make it quite difficult and unpleasant to accuse a sitting member of Congress of sexual harassment.
sentences.zh: 所以她们描述的这套系统，似乎让指控一位在任国会议员性骚扰变得非常困难且令人不快。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I think people who have gone through this or are thinking about this or decline to do this do not see much upside to it.
sentences.zh: 我认为经历过这一切，或者正在考虑，或者拒绝这样做的人，都看不到什么好处。

sentences.en: To refer to pop culture, it is a house of cards.
sentences.zh: 用流行文化的话说，这就是一座纸牌屋。

sentences.en: What's the incentive to take down your boss and what does your future look like?
sentences.zh: 扳倒你的老板有什么激励措施？你的未来会是什么样？

sentences.en: And then also how much does it cost?
sentences.zh: 还有，这要付出多少代价？

sentences.en: What does it cost you in the office?
sentences.zh: 在办公室里要付出什么代价？

sentences.en: What does it cost your reputation?
sentences.zh: 对你的名誉有什么影响？

sentences.en: A lot of women who come here when they're in their 20s and make $27,000 a year don't really see the upshot in going through a three-month expensive process in one of the most gossipy workplaces on earth.
sentences.zh: 许多20多岁来到这里、年薪27,000美元的女性，真的看不出在世界上最爱嚼舌根的职场之一经历三个月昂贵流程的意义。

sentences.en: And what happens if a member of Congress is determined through this very long and unpleasant process to have done something wrong?
sentences.zh: 如果一名国会议员通过这个漫长且令人不快的程序被认定做了错事，会发生什么？

sentences.en: If there is a settlement reached, it's still confidential.
sentences.zh: 如果达成了和解，它仍然是保密的。

sentences.en: It's not reported that this lawmaker is settled againSt.
sentences.zh: 外界不会知道这位议员再次达成了和解。

sentences.en: And the U.S.
sentences.zh: 而且美国财政部支付这笔和解金。

sentences.en: Treasury pays for the settlement.
sentences.zh: 所以纳税人实际上是在为针对议员的和解买单。

sentences.en: So taxpayers essentially pay for a settlement against a lawmaker.
sentences.zh: 我糊涂了。

sentences.en: I'm confused.
sentences.zh: 纳税人在支付经济和解金，但由于保密性，却从未被告知发生了和解，对吗？

sentences.en: The taxpayer is paying for a financial settlement but is never told that a settlement has occurred given the secrecy, right?
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 基本上，如果你所在选区的议员做了这样的错事，你是不会知道的。

sentences.en: Basically, if your lawmaker in your district has done something wrong like this, you will not know about it.
sentences.zh: 我们知道为什么会这样吗？

sentences.en: And do we know why that's the case?
sentences.zh: 这就是规则。

sentences.en: Those are the rules.
sentences.zh: 制度就是这样设定的。

sentences.en: That's how it's set up.
sentences.zh: 那么，国会山这场传达了所有这些骚扰故事的听证会，结论是否是这套系统显然已经崩溃，并阻碍了女性站出来？

sentences.en: So was the conclusion of this hearing on Capitol Hill where all of these stories were conveyed about harassment that this system is quite clearly broken and discourages women from coming forward?
sentences.zh: 上周，来自纽约的参议员克里斯汀·吉利布兰德和来自加州的众议员杰基·斯皮尔，以及其他几位议员，

sentences.en: So last week, Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, she's of New York, and Congresswoman Jackie Speier of California, along with several other lawmakers,
sentences.zh: 提出了他们所谓的《Me Too国会法案》，除其他事项外，该法案将要求议员办公室支付和解金，而不是由美国财政部支付。

sentences.en: introduced what they're calling the Me Too Congress Act, which would, among other things, require for a lawmaker's office to pay settlements and not the U.S.
sentences.zh: 它将使报告过程变为可选择保密。

sentences.en: Treasury.
sentences.zh: 所以如果有人想公开，他们可以这样做。

sentences.en: It would make the reporting process optionally confidential.
sentences.zh: 它将要求任何支付的和解金都在合规办公室的网站上公布。

sentences.en: So if somebody wanted to take things public, they could.
sentences.zh: 这将从一个完全不透明的过程转变为超级透明和公开。

sentences.en: And it would require any settlements paid to be published on the Office of Compliance website.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: It would go from a completely opaque process to being super transparent and out in the open.
sentences.zh: 不客气。

sentences.en: Katie, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，是参议员克里斯汀·吉利布兰德。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: After the break, Senator Kirsten Gillibrand.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最有影响力的领导人，包括J.D.万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯汀·拉加德、扎伊兰·蒙达尼等等。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日直播部分采访，供大家在NYTimes.com免费观看。

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并获得一个月的免费访问权限，阅读我们所有的报道。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 不过，这种情况已经持续一段时间了。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我从来不觉得我可以大声说，哦，我很好，或者我没事。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 总是说，嗯，每天都有艰难的事情发生。

sentences.en: It's been that way for a while, though.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I never feel like I could say, oh, I'm great or I'm fine.
sentences.zh: 真的，从选举以来就是这样。

sentences.en: It's always, well, tough things are happening every day.
sentences.zh: 上周四，也就是她提出解决国会山性不端行为立法的同一天，

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 来自纽约的参议员克里斯汀·吉利布兰德与我的同事詹妮弗·斯坦豪尔坐下来进行了交谈。

sentences.en: Since, really, since the election.
sentences.zh: 自从你第一次来到国会山，你看到了多少变化？

sentences.en: On Thursday of last week, the same day that she introduced legislation to address sexual misconduct on Capitol Hill,
sentences.zh: 作为一名议员和女性议员，你观察到的最大变化是什么？

sentences.en: Senator Kirsten Gillibrand of New York sat down with my colleague Jennifer Steinhauer.
sentences.zh: 嗯，关于性侵犯和性骚扰的辩论在过去五年里愈演愈烈。

sentences.en: Since you first arrived at the Hill, how much have you seen change?
sentences.zh: 目前它已经扩散到整个社会。

sentences.en: What would you observe as the biggest changes that you've noted as a lawmaker and as a female lawmaker?
sentences.zh: 但我认为有些事情将会改变。

sentences.en: Well, this debate about sexual assault, sexual harassment has only grown in the last five years.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个清算的时刻。

sentences.en: It's really metastasized into all of society at this point.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个真正可能实现问责制的时刻。

sentences.en: But I think something is going to change.
sentences.zh: 但我们必须继续战斗。

sentences.en: I think this is a reckoning moment.
sentences.zh: 你与校园性侵犯等问题有着非常紧密的联系。

sentences.en: I think it is a time when accountability is actually possible.
sentences.zh: 而你现在也参与关注国会山的性骚扰问题。

sentences.en: But we have to keep fighting.
sentences.zh: 参议员，你认为这些机构之间有什么共同点吗？

sentences.en: So you are very closely associated with issues around assault on campuses, sexual assault.
sentences.zh: 这与权力有关吗？

sentences.en: And you are now involved in looking at sexual harassment here on the Hill.
sentences.zh: 在处理这些问题时，你觉得什么是非常熟悉的？

sentences.en: What, Senator, do you see as sort of a common thread with all these institutionally?
sentences.zh: 是的，有一个巨大的共同点。

sentences.en: Does it have to do with power?
sentences.zh: 机构保护内部的权势人物。

sentences.en: What do you see working on these issues that is very familiar?
sentences.zh: 在国会，这里的程序绝大多数情况下是在保护国会议员。

sentences.en: Yes, it is a huge common thread.
sentences.zh: 他们强迫被骚扰的人在被允许举报之前，必须与骚扰者进行数月的调解。

sentences.en: Institutions protect the powerful within them.
sentences.zh: 这就是那种非常成问题的系统性偏见。

sentences.en: In Congress, the process here overwhelmingly protects Congress members.
sentences.zh: 看看其他机构。

sentences.en: They force the person who has been harassed to sit in a mediation for months with a harasser before she's even allowed to report it.
sentences.zh: 看看好莱坞，所有那些女性被迫签署的保密协议。

sentences.en: That's the kind of systemic bias that's really problematic.
sentences.zh: 看看华尔街。

sentences.en: You look at other institutions.
sentences.zh: 看看任何存在偏袒权势者、偏袒掠夺者、偏袒现状的制度性偏见的地方。

sentences.en: You look at Hollywood, all the nondisclosure agreements that women were forced to sign.
sentences.zh: 你都不会拥有透明度或问责制。

sentences.en: You look at Wall Street.
sentences.zh: 你都不会拥有透明度或问责制。

sentences.en: You look at any place where you have institutional bias in favor of the powerful, in favor of the predator, in favor of the status quo.
sentences.zh: 你都不会拥有透明度或问责制。

sentences.en: You don't have transparency or accountability.
sentences.zh: 你都不会拥有透明度或问责制。

sentences.en: I want to unpack some of the complications around harassment in the workplace, around the things that you've recounted personally.
sentences.zh: 我想梳理一下职场性骚扰中一些复杂的问题，特别是你个人亲身经历过的那些事。

sentences.en: You recounted in your book about a senior senator making a comment about your weight, saying, don't lose too much weight.
sentences.zh: 你在书中提到，一位资深参议员曾对你的体重发表评论，说：别减太多体重。

sentences.en: I like my girls chubby.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢我的女孩胖乎乎的。

sentences.en: So one thing I want to ask you, spending all the time you have as an elected official on
sentences.zh: 所以我想问你一个问题，作为一名民选官员，你把所有时间都花在

sentences.en: the Hill and coming from the background that you did in New York, you know, very male-dominated professions, was that your first experience with harassment?
sentences.zh: 国会山上，而且你之前在纽约从事的是那种男性主导的职业，那是你第一次经历性骚扰吗？

sentences.en: Well, interestingly, I didn't see it that way just because I didn't feel intimidated or I didn't feel attacked because he was a peer.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有趣的是，我当时并不觉得那是性骚扰，因为我没有感到被恐吓或被攻击，毕竟他也是我的同僚。

sentences.en: I certainly felt that way when I was a young associate in a law firm.
sentences.zh: 但我在律师事务所当年轻律师时，确实有过那种感觉。

sentences.en: I shared one instance in my book where the partner I was working for, after years of working on a case, we're having a celebratory dinner and he's recounting in a speech all the
sentences.zh: 我在书中分享过一个例子：我为一位合伙人工作多年，在一个案子结束后，我们举行了庆祝晚宴，他在演讲中细数了

sentences.en: good works of different people on the team.
sentences.zh: 团队中不同成员的贡献。

sentences.en: And when he gets to me, he said, oh, Kirsten's in such a wonderful job, but don't you just love her haircut?
sentences.zh: 当轮到我时，他说：哦，克尔斯滕工作做得真棒，但难道你不觉得她的发型很可爱吗？

sentences.en: Doesn't she just look amazing?
sentences.zh: 她看起来难道不迷人吗？

sentences.en: And I could have died at that moment because he was reducing all the work I'd done for years to my haircut.
sentences.zh: 那一刻我简直想找个地缝钻进去，因为他把我多年来的所有工作成果都归结为我的发型。

sentences.en: I mean, that's demoralizing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这太打击人了。

sentences.en: And I think experiences that women have in the workplace, particularly when you're younger, when you don't necessarily have all the tools or confidence to know it's not about you,
sentences.zh: 我认为女性在职场中，尤其是年轻时，往往没有足够的经验或自信去意识到这并不是你的问题，

sentences.en: it's about them, that they're the one in the wrong.
sentences.zh: 而是他们的问题，是他们做错了。

sentences.en: It's not you.
sentences.zh: 不是你的错。

sentences.en: It's not your performance.
sentences.zh: 不是你的表现问题。

sentences.en: It's not your ability.
sentences.zh: 也不是你的能力问题。

sentences.en: That's the harder thing.
sentences.zh: 这才是最难接受的部分。

sentences.en: And that's why I shared all those stories because I really wanted that young reader to read my book and say, even if someone does that to me in the workplace, I can push past it.
sentences.zh: 所以我分享了所有这些故事，因为我真心希望年轻的读者在读我的书时能明白，即使在职场中有人这样对待我，我也能克服它。

sentences.en: I can start my own business.
sentences.zh: 我可以开始自己的事业。

sentences.en: I can be a partner someday and change the climate, but I can do something about it.
sentences.zh: 我将来可以成为合伙人并改变这种氛围，我可以采取行动。

sentences.en: It doesn't define me.
sentences.zh: 这并不能定义我。

sentences.en: And it's not a reflection on me.
sentences.zh: 这也不是我的问题。

sentences.en: It's a reflection on them and what's wrong with them.
sentences.zh: 这是他们的问题，是他们自身出了毛病。

sentences.en: That's the whole point.
sentences.zh: 这才是重点。

sentences.en: I remember at the time when that book came out, because I was a female reporter on the Hill, and this was very talked about, and there was some dissent, right, in the press corps.
sentences.zh: 我记得那本书出版时，因为我当时是国会山的女性记者，这件事讨论得非常热烈，新闻界内部也存在一些异议，对吧？

sentences.en: And I'm not going to say it was totally male-female lines, but it sort of was, where, oh, I don't believe that happened.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说这完全是按男女阵营划分的，但确实有点像，有人会说：哦，我不相信那是真的。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Or a little bit, or, oh, gosh, was it that big a deal?
sentences.zh: 或者说：哦，天哪，这算什么大事吗？

sentences.en: So I'm curious if you heard any of that, what you thought about it at the time.
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇你是否听到过这些言论，当时你是怎么想的？

sentences.en: And do you think that that same reaction is even possible just a few years later in the context that we're in right now?
sentences.zh: 你认为在几年后的今天，在当前的背景下，同样的反应还会出现吗？

sentences.en: What the Me Too movement has done is transform this debate, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为“我也是”（Me Too）运动已经彻底改变了这场辩论。

sentences.en: Because when you have hundreds and thousands of people coming out every day about all industries saying,
sentences.zh: 因为当每天都有成百上千的人站出来，讲述各行各业发生的事情，说：

sentences.en: this is what happened to me, I think a lot of people have finally realized, wow, I didn't quite realize this.
sentences.zh: 这就是发生在我身上的事，我想很多人终于意识到：哇，我以前真的没意识到这一点。

sentences.en: And so they can't necessarily imagine it happening to them, but I can imagine it happening every time.
sentences.zh: 他们可能无法想象这种事发生在自己身上，但我每次都能想象得到。

sentences.en: I can absolutely imagine each of these stories happening and also imagining the heartbreak that that person feels
sentences.zh: 我完全能想象这些故事中的每一个，也能想象当事人所感受到的心碎，

sentences.en: and that the fact that they really don't recover, you don't really move on when you've been marginalized, attacked, or harassed.
sentences.zh: 以及一旦你被边缘化、被攻击或被骚扰，你其实很难真正恢复，很难真正走出来。

sentences.en: Now, in terms of how the complicated way that women relate to people who have harassed them or have these incidents at work,
sentences.zh: 那么，关于女性如何处理与骚扰者或职场骚扰事件的关系，这种方式很复杂，

sentences.en: you know, you did not name the senator in your book, and I noticed that in Testimony on the Hill,
sentences.zh: 你知道，你在书中没有点出那位参议员的名字，我注意到在国会山的证词中，

sentences.en: Congresswomen have chosen not to name members of Congress that they say are still actually in Congress, in office.
sentences.zh: 女议员们选择不点名那些她们声称仍在国会任职的议员。

sentences.en: What about that?
sentences.zh: 对此你怎么看？

sentences.en: I mean, are women still in a protective mode with their male colleagues, or are they self-protecting women?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，女性是在保护她们的男性同事，还是在进行自我保护？

sentences.en: Part of the whole Me Too movement obviously was sparked by people who were willing to name their harassers by name.
sentences.zh: 显然，“我也是”运动的部分动力来自于那些愿意公开骚扰者姓名的人。

sentences.en: So what do you think?
sentences.zh: 所以你觉得呢？

sentences.en: So I leave it to the survivors.
sentences.zh: 所以我把决定权留给受害者。

sentences.en: They should decide whether or not they want to name the harasser.
sentences.zh: 她们应该自己决定是否要公开骚扰者的名字。

sentences.en: And the way we rewrote our bill, so we have a bill now to change how the process here on the Hill works.
sentences.zh: 我们重写了法案，现在我们有一项法案旨在改变国会山的处理流程。

sentences.en: One of the things is, is put it in the survivors' hands.
sentences.zh: 其中一点就是把权力交到受害者手中。

sentences.en: Because right now they're forced to sign nondisclosure agreements so that if there is a settlement, they can't even talk about it.
sentences.zh: 因为目前她们被迫签署保密协议，一旦达成和解，她们甚至不能谈论这件事。

sentences.en: I change that and let the survivor decide whether or not they want to talk about it.
sentences.zh: 我改变了这一点，让受害者决定是否要谈论它。

sentences.en: Because those rules are set up to protect the Congress members.
sentences.zh: 因为那些规则的设立初衷就是为了保护国会议员。

sentences.en: On Friday, Congresswoman Jackie Speier, who co-sponsored the Me Too legislation with Gillibrand,
sentences.zh: 周五，与吉利布兰德共同发起“我也是”立法的女议员杰基·斯皮尔，

sentences.en: posted a video to her YouTube page telling her story of sexual harassment on Capitol Hill.
sentences.zh: 在她的YouTube页面上发布了一段视频，讲述了她在国会山遭受性骚扰的经历。

sentences.en: Like so many of you, I have a Me Too story to share.
sentences.zh: 和你们许多人一样，我也有一个“我也是”的故事要分享。

sentences.en: I was working as a congressional staffer.
sentences.zh: 当时我是一名国会工作人员。

sentences.en: The chief of staff held my face, kissed me, and stuck his tongue in my mouth.
sentences.zh: 幕僚长捧着我的脸，亲吻我，并把舌头伸进我的嘴里。

sentences.en: So I know what it's like to keep these things hidden deep down inside.
sentences.zh: 所以我知道把这些事情深埋在心底是什么滋味。

sentences.en: I know what it's like to lie awake in bed at night wondering if I was the one who had done something wrong.
sentences.zh: 我知道晚上躺在床上辗转反侧，怀疑是不是自己做错了什么是什么滋味。

sentences.en: I know what it's like years later to remember that rush of humiliation and anger.
sentences.zh: 我知道多年后回想起那种屈辱和愤怒的冲击是什么滋味。

sentences.en: You know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: Many of us in Congress know what it's like.
sentences.zh: 我们国会中的许多人都知道这是什么滋味。

sentences.en: Because Congress has been a breeding ground for a hostile work environment for far too long.
sentences.zh: 因为国会长期以来一直是滋生敌对工作环境的温床。

sentences.en: On Monday, after Congresswoman Jackie Speier posted this video, and after Jennifer Steinhauer's interview with Senator Gillibrand,
sentences.zh: 周一，在杰基·斯皮尔议员发布这段视频后，以及詹妮弗·斯坦豪尔采访吉利布兰德参议员之后，

sentences.en: a second woman came forward to accuse their Democratic colleague, Senator Al Franken,
sentences.zh: 第二位女性站出来指控她们的民主党同僚、参议员阿尔·弗兰肯，

sentences.en: of inappropriately touching her at the Minnesota State Fair in 2010 while he was in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 称他在2010年担任参议员期间，在明尼苏达州博览会上对她进行不当触摸。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的消息。

sentences.en: Eight women have told the Washington Post that TV host Charlie Rose made unwanted sexual advances toward them,
sentences.zh: 八名女性告诉《华盛顿邮报》，电视主持人查理·罗斯曾对她们进行不受欢迎的性挑逗，

sentences.en: including lewd phone calls walking around naked in their presence and groping them.
sentences.zh: 包括打淫秽电话、在她们面前赤身裸体走动以及猥亵她们。

sentences.en: PBS quickly suspended distribution of the Charlie Rose show, and CBS said it had suspended Rose as co-host of CBS This Morning,
sentences.zh: 美国公共广播公司（PBS）迅速停止了《查理·罗斯访谈录》的发行，哥伦比亚广播公司（CBS）表示已暂停罗斯作为《CBS今晨》联合主持人的职务，

sentences.en: where he has been covering the sexual harassment allegations against men like Harvey Weinstein and Bill O'Reilly,
sentences.zh: 而他此前一直在报道针对哈维·温斯坦和比尔·奥莱利等男性的性骚扰指控，

sentences.en: and recently spoke to my colleague, Emily Steele, about her reporting on the issue.
sentences.zh: 最近还与我的同事艾米丽·斯蒂尔谈论过她关于此议题的报道。

sentences.en: And how are corporations changing?
sentences.zh: 企业正在发生怎样的变化？

sentences.en: How are institutions changing?
sentences.zh: 机构正在发生怎样的变化？

sentences.en: And what is, I mean, it's such a historic change.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这真是一场历史性的变革。

sentences.en: What is the emerging definition of sexual harassment?
sentences.zh: 性骚扰的新定义是什么？

sentences.en: Well, that's one thing that we've talked a lot about, is that the actual legal definition of sexual harassment is quite gray,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是我们讨论过很多的一个问题，即性骚扰的实际法律定义相当模糊，

sentences.en: and that there are these standards that the behavior needs to be severe and pervasive and have a negative impact on your career in order to bring a legal case.
sentences.zh: 而且要提起法律诉讼，行为必须达到严重且普遍，并对你的职业生涯产生负面影响的标准。

sentences.en: The accusations come from women who worked for Rose or aspired to work for him on The Charlie Rose Show from the late 1990s to as recently as 2011.
sentences.zh: 这些指控来自从20世纪90年代末到2011年期间为罗斯工作或渴望在《查理·罗斯访谈录》节目中为他工作的女性。

sentences.en: In a statement, Rose apologized, saying, quote,
sentences.zh: 罗斯在一份声明中道歉，称，引用如下：

sentences.en: I am greatly embarrassed.
sentences.zh: 我感到非常尴尬。

sentences.en: I have behaved insensitively at times, and I accept responsibility for that, though I do not believe that all of these allegations are accurate.
sentences.zh: 我有时表现得不够敏感，我对此承担责任，尽管我不认为所有这些指控都是准确的。

sentences.en: I always felt that I was pursuing shared feelings, even though I now realize I was mistaken.
sentences.zh: 我一直觉得我是在追求共同的情感，尽管我现在意识到我错了。

sentences.en: And Glenn Thrush, a White House reporter for The Times, has been suspended after four female journalists accused him of inappropriate sexual behavior.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》白宫记者格伦·思拉什在四名女记者指控他有不当性行为后已被停职。

sentences.en: Finally, the Trump administration is ending a humanitarian program that has allowed 59,000 residents of Haiti to live and work in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 最后，特朗普政府正在结束一项人道主义计划，该计划曾允许5.9万名海地居民在美国生活和工作，

sentences.en: after the earthquake that ravaged their country in 2010.
sentences.zh: 这是在2010年海地发生毁灭性地震之后实施的。

sentences.en: By July of next year, those Haitians will be forced to leave the U.S.
sentences.zh: 到明年七月，这些海地人将被迫离开美国，

sentences.en: or face deportation.
sentences.zh: 否则将面临驱逐出境。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目，我们准备讨论假期招待客人的事宜。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人感到宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they black out to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线条件？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on The New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何播客平台上收听《Wirecutter秀》。
